description: We’re a team of science, tech, and econ undergraduate students from Indonesia taking on the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge at the Purwokerto local event. Our skills cover fullstack development, machine learning, deep learning, game development, UI/UX, cybersecurity, research, and storytelling. Our core roles are covered, but if you’re strong in visual design, illustration, motion graphics or 3D art, we’d be glad to have you join us!
summary: Phantom Worlds is a public website that turns NASA's SPHEREx infrared survey into a sky anyone can explore. SPHEREx maps the whole sky every six months in 102 infrared bands, which is exactly where a cold, faint world near the Sun, such as an undiscovered brown dwarf or a distant planet, would show itself: dark in visible light, bright only at long infrared wavelengths, and moving between visits. The data is public but arrives as hundreds of thousands of separate frames, so spotting change by hand is slow. Phantom Worlds lets people pan and zoom the real SPHEREx all-sky map like a map app, play through its wavelength bands, read any position's light across 102 bands, and share what looks unusual. The community votes on each find, and approved scientists review the strongest ones. It makes a new NASA dataset searchable by many eyes, with honest labelling of what is measured and what is estimated.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Phantom Worlds connects a sky viewer, a data panel, a community forum and a scientist review queue into one path from a patch of sky to a reviewed find.

1. Sky Explorer: the real SPHEREx DR1 all-sky mosaic, drawn directly from NASA/IPAC IRSA map tiles. Users drag and zoom from the whole sky down to single mosaic pixels, switch between the six detectors or a false-colour view, and play through each detector's wavelength bands. Coordinates of the view centre and the cursor are always shown.

2. Data panel: click any point to read its brightness in all 102 bands, plus, for pipeline-detected signals, the probability that it is real, signal to noise, motion, change between visits and molecule signatures (water ice, methane, CO2, CO).

3. Share your find: one form posts a position with its readings attached and checks for duplicates within 10 arcseconds.

4. Discussions: the community votes and comments, linking comments to specific frames. Ten up votes send a find to review.

5. Labs: approved scientists (verified by ORCID iD) review the full data and accept a find or close it as a false positive, a known object or too faint. Accepted finds enter a public Community Catalog with downloadable data.

6. Proof: a public report card of our pipeline's tests, including the ones it fails.

HOW IT WORKS

Our pipeline searches SPHEREx frames for leftover residuals, variable sources and movers, aligns them against Gaia DR3, and scores each signal with a real-or-artifact model and a type model. The website shows those results and lets people check them by eye.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

- Opens a brand-new NASA dataset to students, amateurs and citizen scientists with no setup.

- Puts many human eyes on candidates that automated searches flag but cannot judge alone.

- Gives scientists a filtered queue instead of raw frames.

- Builds trust through honesty: every number shows its unit, its uncertainty and whether it was measured, taken from a catalogue, estimated or assumed. Model outputs always say "Estimated" and use fixed confidence words. Words like "Confirmed" and "Discovery" are reserved for outside confirmation.

TOOLS AND LANGUAGES

Frontend: HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no framework, including our own HEALPix tile renderer for the SPHEREx all-sky HiPS cube, written because existing viewers could not read its layout.

Pipeline and backend: Python, FastAPI, Astropy, photutils, scikit-learn, SciPy and NumPy.

Design: a written UI specification, accessibility checks and responsive layouts for desktop and phone.

CREATIVITY

- A map-style viewer for the real 102-band sky, with wavelength playback, instead of a static image.

- A spectrum strip that turns 102 bands into one coloured bar you can read at a glance.

- Blind-first review and a progress bar to review make the community step fair and visible.

- Gamification that rewards being right over being busy: XP and reputation are separate, levels are named after real stars from hot to cold, and there is no global leaderboard.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Scientific honesty, accessibility (keyboard use, contrast, reduced motion, 44 px touch targets), performance on ordinary phones, clear plain-language wording, the difference between real and simulated data (always labelled), and responsible review so nothing is called a discovery before experts check it.
